articles.title: The rise of Cooper Flagg: How the Mavericks' teenage star is leading the franchise forward
articles.summary: With the teenage star's continued trajectory, Dallas' future is much brighter than its recent past.
articles.body:
DALLAS — Not long after an emotional NBA Cup win over the Houston Rockets on Friday, Cooper Flagg was asked about the joys of the Dallas' Mavericks' new two-star dynamic. Flagg and Kyrie Irving had combined for 68 points, 15 assists and 13 rebounds in the contest, the Mavs' third win in a row. But the 19-year-old didn't want to focus on himself or take away from his team's achievement against a legitimate contender.

Flagg redirected the question to preach about players excelling in their various roles regardless of perceived status.

Such a remark can be lost in a postgame interview, especially one where the subject tends to keep things brief and direct. But in that moment, Flagg was displaying a level of leadership that is typically unbeknownst to teenagers, much less budding superstars being handed the keys to a franchise.

In three months, it will mark two years since the stunning Dallas trade that sent Luka Dončić to Los Angeles in exchange for Anthony Davis. The massive void left by Dončić and the emotional toll from such a jarring move created a butterfly effect for the city and organization, ultimately leading to the drafting of Flagg, but also the firing of head coach Jason Kidd and general manager Nico Harrison, and the hiring of Dusty May and Masai Ujiri this offseason.

But beauty can emerge from despair. So when May and Ujiri embraced in the tunnel after the final buzzer against Houston, hope re-emerged. And although the transition between eras has certainly come with its fair share of detours, Flagg's growing leadership in Year 2 — and, more importantly, his veteran teammates empowering him — has provided a North Star to follow.

"He's taken a step into a leadership role," teammate Daniel Gafford said. "There's different ways you can lead in certain areas. With Coop, he just finds ways to have fun throughout the craziest times. Kyrie [Irving] is one of the biggest leaders in the locker room and he leads by his voice and example. Coop is following suit and taking notes and doing it himself."

"It's huge," Flagg added. "Just getting the respect of my peers and teammates last year was big for me. They're trusting me, I'm trusting myself. It's a good recipe."

Flagg's mental growth has been concurrent with his on-court development. In the shot clock era, there are only 20 players who have averaged 25 points, 5 rebounds, 5 assists, a steal and a block per game. At 19, Flagg is the youngest ever to reach those benchmarks.

Ironically, part of his success stems from the chaos he was born into. As a rookie under Kidd, Flagg was originally miscast as a point guard with questionable spacing at times, and at other junctures shared a backcourt with the likes of Brandon Williams, Ryan Nembhard and D'Angelo Russell — hardly a trio of names that screams development. Flagg also was a victim of Dallas' rotational roulette; only Cleveland and Washington had their most common lineups on the floor together less than Flagg's most consistent one (92 minutes, per NBA.com tracking data) last season.

A year later, Flagg has a clear-cut role in a cleaner half-court setup and has taken lessons from his playmaking past and refined them. His processor has sped up as the game has slowed down for him, better understanding how to attack opposing defenders, crack open schemes and create the best shot for himself and those around him.

As his usage rate has risen, so too has his assist rate, with Flagg now operating in the 98th and 97th percentiles , respectively, per Cleaning the Glass. An increase in possessions as a ball-handler has resulted in top-20 marks in secondary assists, potential assists and assist points created. It's no surprise the Mavericks are 17 points per 100 half-court possessions better with Flagg on the floor.

Flip to a Mavs game on League Pass on a Tuesday night and you'll see Irving receive an inbounds pass, flip it to Flagg and jog to the opposing wing to let him go to work.

"Just comfortable," Flagg said on how he feels with the ball in the half-court. "I'm comfortable getting to my spots and with my teammates. Coach is putting me in great spots."

Dallas was one of the worst spacing units last season, but Flagg now has Irving (a career 40% 3-point shooter) and Max Christie (38%) next to him (and the hope is P.J. Washington returns to his 2024 form, where he shot 38% from deep). May also wants to play with pace and incorporates a high volume of pick-and-rolls to get both Flagg and Irving on the ball. The pace, space and freedom allow Flagg's unorthodox style to take form — more isolations , more midrange attempts and a better overall shot selection. (His 3-point efficiency, hovering around 23%, remains a work in progress, but he's been able to establish elite go-to moves that negate the need to launch unnecessary 3s into the sun.)

Flagg's improved comfort within the offense speaks to his relationship with May; an open, honest one that incorporates feedback and fluidity.

"It's been great," Flagg said of his bond with May. "He watched a ton of film from last year and knows my game pretty well. So just whatever he's seeing where he wants to put me, it's been working really well."

Still, arguably none of this is made possible without Irving's presence, patience and poise. For starters, his gravity alone makes Flagg's job easier on a nightly basis, drawing attention away from him and opening up more space to operate. But Irving's experience, having shared the spotlight with a plethora of big names during his tenure, makes the day-to-day easier as well. For what it's worth, the Mavericks have outscored opponents by 25 points in 98 minutes that Flagg and Irving have been on the floor together. It's been less of a turn-by-turn approach and more cooperative, with Irving wanting to push Flagg to be the best version of himself. As an elder statesman now, it's about giving back to the younger generation.

"It's been great," Irving said to Yahoo Sports. "In my first few years in the league, I had some good veterans — Anthony Parker, Antawn Jamison, Anderson Varejão — they were all good to me. But I was always trying to figure out what more I can do to bring to the team, and the best thing for me was being able to be honest about who I wanted to become in this league and how I was gonna accomplish it. It wasn't a solo job. I think he has a lot more patience than I did when I was his age. With the supporting cast around him, he can trust us with any information or questions he wants to ask."

It takes a village to raise young players. A head coach without NBA experience forced to lean on his roster, creativity and communication. A wily, sage veteran with championship experience that is hell-bent on pouring into the next phase of NBA basketball. A community that supports and sees the full potential of an ascending superstar.

There's still work to do. The Mavericks, despite their winning record, are just 18th in net rating. And it's not just their conference that remains a gauntlet; their own division — with the Rockets, Spurs and Grizzlies ahead of them — is as deep as ever. But with Flagg's continued trajectory , along with the other now-stable pieces in place, Dallas' future is much brighter than its recent past.

"There's always so much room for improvement," Flagg said. "I haven't shot the ball incredibly well behind the arc. But just continuing to play at my own pace, getting better and cleaning up the turnovers. There's always room for improvement."

articles.title: Kon Knueppel Injured in Season Debut, Latest on Hornets Star After Exiting vs. Nets
articles.summary: Charlotte Hornets forward Kon Knueppel did not last long in his first game of the season.
articles.body:
Charlotte Hornets forward Kon Knueppel did not last long in his first game of the season.

After making his season debut against the Brooklyn Nets on Wednesday, lasted only six minutes before being ruled out with "leg soreness," the team announced:

Every NBA Team's Biggest Problem Right Now 😠

He had just three points before exiting in the first quarter.

Knueppel has been sidelined by a hamstring strain he suffered during offseason workouts in September. The injury forced the 21-year-old to miss the entire preseason and all eight of Charlotte's games to the start of the 2026-27 season.

The latest setback is another disappointment for a team that has struggled to find its footing so far this season. After winning three of their first four games, the Hornets lost four consecutive games heading into their matchup against Brooklyn and ranked dead last in scoring offense.

The team's struggles can partially be explained by the absence of Knueppel and starting guard Coby White. Knueppel at full strength could help Charlotte get its season back on track, although there are now more questions about his health.

Knueppel was selected with the No. 4 overall pick in the 2025 NBA Draft and dazzled during his rookie campaign. He earned NBA All-Rookie First Team honors and finished second in NBA Rookie of the Year voting behind Cooper Flagg. Knueppel finished the season with 273 made three-pointers, making him the first rookie to lead the league in three-pointers made in NBA history.

articles.title: Juwan Howard sells newly built Coral Gables mansion for $25 million, below its $28.9 million asking price; former NBA star bought the 1.73-acre property for $3.4 million in 2013
articles.summary: Former NBA star and two-time champion Juwan Howard has sold his newly built mansion in Coral Gables, Florida, for $25 million.
articles.body: Former NBA star and two-time champion Juwan Howard has sold his newly built mansion in Coral Gables, Florida, for $25 million. The property, located in the exclusive gated community of Journey’s End, was being marketed for US$28.9 million (approximately A$40.5 million) in June before eventually selling for a lower price.According to a report by The Wall Street Journal, Howard fetched $25 million for the property. Lauren Schrager and Toni Schrager of Brown Harris Stevens represented the former basketball player in the deal. Lauren Schrager reportedly declined to comment on the buyer’s identity.The buyer was represented by Carla Defortuna and Carolina Cuadra of Fortune Christie’s International Real Estate. Howard, who is currently an assistant coach with the Brooklyn Nets, did not respond to the publication’s request for comment.Inside Juwan Howard’s $25 million Coral Gables mansionDesigned by renowned Miami architect Kobi Karp, the contemporary estate sits on a 1.73-acre plot at 9440 Old Cutler Lane in Coral Gables. The seven-bedroom residence has a living area of 8,997 square feet and a total building area of 10,117 square feet. Based on the total building area, the property sold for approximately $2,471 per square foot.The mansion's interiors feature a dramatic double-height foyer with a floating staircase and soaring 23-foot ceilings. Floor-to-ceiling glass brings natural light into the living spaces, while limestone flooring connects the formal living room, dining area and family room. The house also features a Snaidero kitchen, adding to its contemporary design.The upper level houses the primary suite, which occupies its own wing and includes walk-in closets and spa-inspired bathrooms. The other bedrooms are designed as en-suite spaces, while additional rooms can be used for entertainment, work or recreation.The estate also comes with a wellness suite, wine room and media room. Outside, a 75-by-25-foot resort-style swimming pool overlooks the landscaped grounds, which give the property the feel of a private park. A detached four-car garage is another feature of the residence.Private marina access and an exclusive gated communityThe mansion is located in Journey’s End, an exclusive residential enclave comprising just 18 estates. The gated community offers 24-hour security, two tennis courts and access to a private marina.The property also comes with a deeded boat slip, a particularly notable feature in South Florida's luxury waterfront market. Its expansive grounds, private pool and access to community amenities add to the appeal of the estate.Juwan Howard bought the property for $3.4 million in 2013Howard purchased the 1.73-acre property in 2013 for approximately $3.4 million. The site originally had a dated 1970s home, which was reportedly demolished to make way for the new residence.Howard subsequently worked with architect Kobi Karp on the custom-built mansion, which was completed in 2026. The estate was initially marketed at $31.5 million in 2025 before its asking price was reduced to $28.9 million in 2026. By June, it was being reported as available at the revised price. It eventually sold for $25 million in November 2026.From Michigan’s Fab Five to a 19-season NBA careerHoward, 53, rose to prominence as a member of the University of Michigan’s famed Fab Five team in the early 1990s. He went on to enjoy a 19-season NBA career, winning two championships and earning one All-Star selection.After retiring as a player, Howard returned to Michigan as head coach, a position he held from 2019 to 2024. He later joined the Brooklyn Nets coaching staff as an assistant coach.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

articles.title: La burrada de Nunn ante el Madrid es récord absoluto de la Euroliga
articles.standfirst: Anotó 23 puntos en un último cuarto sublime
articles.summary: Anotó 23 puntos en un último cuarto sublime
articles.body: Kendrick Nunn llegaba al partido ante el Madrid envuelto en dudas. Desde su llegada, el Panathinaikos había bajado sus prestaciones ofensivas, jugaba más atascado y recibía más puntos en defensa. Pero las grandes estrellas tienen esas cosas. Ha vuelto de una lesión larga y en Madrid demostró que está al su nivel habitual, ganando casi él solo el partido. El Panathinaikos ganó en Madrid por dos cosas. Acertó más en los triples y tuvo a Nunn de su lado. El estadounidense, que se fue hasta los 33 puntos, firmó 23 en un último cuarto sublime. Es récord absoluto en la historia de la Euroliga en un último periodo. Y se queda a tres puntos del tope en cualquier cuarto. Nunn hizo de su actuación un milagro para el PAO. De sus 23 puntos al final, 15 los consiguió en los últimos cinco minutos del tiempo regular, y llegó a encadenar 25 en los últimos 29 puntos de su equipo. Su actuación fue portentosa. Al terminar el partido, Obradovic se deshizo para hablar de su estrella: "Nunca me ha pasado el tener a un jugador que ha jugado más partidos del tiempo que ha entrenado conmigo. No es fácil, pero él (Nunn) es una persona que le encanta el baloncesto. Tiene mucha calidad. Era una cuestión de paciencia. No es fácil volver después de un parón por lesión de dos o tres meses. Ha hecho un partido fantástico en ataque". En defensa, al final, Bonga era el que salía por él.

articles.title: Watch LeBron James Make NBA History with New Career Milestone During 76ers vs. Pistons
articles.summary: Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James became the first player in NBA history to amass 16,000 career field goals when he made a layup early in the second quarter of his team's road game against the Detroit Pistons on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James became the first player in NBA history to amass 16,000 career field goals when he made a layup early in the second quarter of his team's road game against the Detroit Pistons on Wednesday.

Entering the evening, James needed to make two shots to hit the 16,000 mark. He got it done early on and gave the 76ers a 33-23 lead as well.

James surpassed Basketball Hall of Famer and NBA legend Kareem Abdul-Jabbar for the most made field goals all time last season when the then-Los Angeles Laker hit a jumper in the first quarter of his team's 120-113 loss to the Denver Nuggets on March 5.

Both James and Abdul-Jabbar (15,837 made field goals) are well above the rest of the NBA field, with the next-closet player, Karl Malone, at 13,528 made field goals.

articles.title: AJ Dybantsa Quiet as Hawks Beat Wizards, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Trae Young, AD, Top Players
articles.summary: Atlanta Hawks guard Nickeil Alexander-Walker hit six three-pointers en route to 26 points, and five of his teammates posted double-digits scoring efforts en route to a 120-105 road win over the Washington Wizards on Wednesday evening in the front end of a home-and-home matchup.
articles.body:
Atlanta Hawks guard Nickeil Alexander-Walker hit six three-pointers en route to 26 points, and five of his teammates posted double-digits scoring efforts en route to a 120-105 road win over the Washington Wizards on Wednesday evening in the front end of a home-and-home matchup.

The Hawks were 2.5-point favorites, per FanDuel Sportsbook , but ultimately cleared the spread with ease despite Anthony Davis' 26-point, 10-rebound double-double and the scoring efforts of Kyshawn George (25 points) and Trae Young (18).

Here's a look at the night's top performers.

Wizards rookie forward AJ Dybantsa had an off-night, scoring just nine points on 4-of-12 shooting.

Of course, the 19-year-old (and No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NBA draft) has been very impressive overall, averaging 19.0 points on 50.0 percent shooting in 30 minutes per game over his first three contests leading into Wednesday. Dybantsa also played some catch-up this season after missing the first four games with a left ankle sprain.

As far as the matchup, the storylines can be told from beyond the arc, in the paint and off the bench.

The Hawks made 13 more three-pointers (19-6). Six Hawks hit two or more three-pointers, including Aaron Wiggins, who hit three off the bench en route to his 15 points. Washington only shot 23 percent (6-of-26) from beyond the arc.

Atlanta owned a great rebounding edge (57-41), led by Dyson Daniels' 17 boards. Daniels had seven offensive boards alone, or just two fewer than the entire Wizards team combined. The Hawks finished plus-21 with him on the floor. Onyeka Okongwu added a season-high 16 boards.

Atlanta also scored 52 points off the bench, compared to Washington's 16. Wiggins and CJ McCollum's 15 led the Hawk reserves, but rookie big man Zuby Ejiofor excelled with 11 points in 17 minutes (plus-18).

The 5-4 Hawks and 4-4 Wizards will now complete their home-and-home matchup on Friday at 7 p.m. ET in Atlanta's State Farm Arena.

articles.title: 76ers star Joel Embiid gets technical foul for shoving match with Tolu Smith in win over Pistons
articles.summary: This is Embiid's first technical foul of the regular season.
articles.body:
There were some fireworks with Joel Embiid in the first half at Little Caesars Arena on Wednesday night.

Embiid, who received a technical foul early after a shoving match under the rim, still managed to lead the Philadelphia 76ers to a 112-106 win over the Detroit Pistons. He finished with a double-double with 26 points and 15 rebounds, and powered Philadelphia to an 8-1 record on the year.

But things got heated late in the first half after Jaylen Brown was fouled while shooting under the basket. All of the sudden, as Brown was headed to the free throw line, Embiid got into a shoving match with Detroit's Tolu Smith.

Embiid was jockeying for position with Smith as Brown was working his way to the rim. After the whistle, it looked like Embiid's elbow hit Smith in the chest. Smith then swatted the ball away from Embiid. This led to a shoving match between the two, and in the kerfuffle, Embiid ended up pushing a ref away.

When the dust settled, the refs whistled only Embiid for a technical foul. The Detroit crowd rained down expletives with his last name, and the Philly center stood and egged them on, asking for more.

Pistons point guard Cade Cunningham hit the ensuing free throw from the technical, and Philadelphia went into halftime leading 56-42.

Though the 76ers led by as many as 13 in the final minutes, the Pistons surged late to make it a game. They cut it to just four points after Cunningham hit a layup with 65 seconds left in the contest, but that was as close as they got. Philadelphia held on down the stretch to secure the six-point win.

Embiid shot 8-of-18 from the field and made all 10 of his free throws in the win. The technical was his first of the season. Brown led the way with 30 points and seven assists, and LeBron James finished two assists shy of a triple-double with 13 points, 10 rebounds and eight assists.

Duncan Robinson led the Pistons with 27 points after he went 7-of-11 from the 3-point line. Cunningham had 26 points and 11 assists, and Ausar Thompson had 11 points and 17 rebounds. The Pistons handed the 76ers their lone loss of the season back on Oct. 25. Detroit now sits at 6-2 on the season.

The 76ers and the Pistons will end their three-game season series on February 5.

Embiid has now played in six of the team's games so far this season as the franchise continues to manage his workload to keep him healthy. While things got a bit heated on Wednesday night, Embiid still managed to lift the 76ers to the win without further incident.

articles.title: Stephen Curry Compared to Michael Jordan by Steve Kerr, Warriors' HC Hypes Star's Longevity
articles.summary: Golden State Warriors head coach Steve Kerr offered the highest of praise for Stephen Curry on Wednesday night, saying that coaching him is a similar experience to playing alongside Michael Jordan during his playing career.
articles.body:
Golden State Warriors head coach Steve Kerr offered the highest of praise for Stephen Curry on Wednesday night, saying that coaching him is a similar experience to playing alongside Michael Jordan during his playing career.

"Honestly, it really does remind me of what it was like to play with Michael Jordan back in the day," (8:50 mark). "Every single night you just are amazed and you marvel at what he's capable of doing, no matter what the defense does. But also just the longevity of it. To see night after night, defenses doing everything possible to slow Steph down like they did with Michael, and yet the love for the game, the competitiveness, the passion, the desire to put on a show for the fans—there's such great comparisons to be made there."

LeBron's KD and Steph Scouting Reports 📋

Curry, 38, hasn't lost a step in his 18th season, averaging 30 points, 4.5 assists and 4.2 rebounds per game while shooting 42.9 percent from three. The 5-3 Dubs have been short-handed this season, with Jimmy Butler and Kristaps Porziņģis away from the team due to injuries and medical concerns, but Curry has helped lead them on a five-game winning streak nonetheless.

He was always going to be remembered as the greatest shooter of all time. At this point, however, his career longevity—and the elite level of play he continues to display—is proving to be nearly as impressive.

articles.title: Kon Knueppel leaves season debut with Hornets early with leg injury after offseason hamstring issue
articles.summary: Knueppel missed the preseason and the Hornets' first eight games with a strained left hamstring.
articles.body:
Kon Knueppel's season debut with the Charlotte Hornets didn't go as planned Wednesday night. Knueppel, who had been dealing with a left a hamstring injury in recent weeks, left Charlotte's 114-104 loss to the Brooklyn Nets early due to what the team called a left leg injury. Further specifics are not yet known, but the Hornets quickly ruled him out.

It appeared as if Knueppel pulled up awkwardly while trying to handle the ball on the wing early in the contest. He dribbled the ball off his foot, and then started limping off the floor in significant discomfort.

He had three points and went 0-for-1 shooting from the field in his six minutes on the court at the Barclays Center.

The second-year sharpshooter had yet to play this season due to a strained left hamstring . Knueppel suffered the injury during "offseason on-court activity," the Hornets said in September. He sat out all of the preseason and the team's first eight games.

Last week, Knueppel was assigned to the team's G League affiliate in Greensboro, North Carolina, as part of his recovery. The 21-year-old was initially listed as probable for the Nets game before receiving an upgrade in status hours before tip-off.

Knueppel finished second in NBA Rookie of the Year balloting last season after challenging 2025 No. 1 overall draft pick and eventual winner Cooper Flagg by averaging 18.5 points, 5.3 rebounds and 3.4 assists. Selected No. 4 overall out of Duke in the 2025 NBA Draft , he led the league by making 273 3-pointers, shooting 43% on 673 attempts.

He helped the Hornets improve to 44-38 and earn a spot in the NBA play-in tournament as the No. 9 seed, turning around from the league's third-worst record at 19-63 in 2024-25.

The Nets (2-6) surged ahead in the fourth quarter Wednesday night to grab the 10-point win. Michael Porter Jr. led the way with 26 points and 10 rebounds while shooting 8-of-17 from the field, and Julius Randle added 22 points.

Naz Reid led the Hornets with 28 points and nine rebounds in the loss, which was their fifth straight and dropped them to 3-6 on the season. Grayson Allen added 22 points off the bench, and Brandon Miller finished with 10 points while shooting 2-of-15 from the field.

While specifics of Knueppel's latest injury aren't yet known, losing him for any significant stretch would undoubtedly be a tough development for the Hornets as they get started this season. The team hasn't been to the playoffs in more than a decade, and a healthy Knueppel would be a huge part of that push.

LaMelo Ball shook off early miscues to lead the Wolves past Kevin Durant and the Rockets, 117-107.

The Timberwolves could be without Edwards until at least December, as the star recovers from knee surgery . The absence of an MVP-caliber player like Edwards makes getting off to a strong start quite difficult, and Minnesota will need all the help it can get.

The brunt of the offense will be on Ball, and he struggled for much of the game before finally getting things going in the fourth. Ayo Dosunmu and Bones Hyland did a good job carrying some of the weight on offense, while Ball worked through his early woes.

Durant has had a bit of a slow start to the season by his standards, but he managed to string together a solid performance despite the loss. Meanwhile, Alpereun Sengun posted a triple-double.

The Timberwolves improved to 6-3 with the win, while the Rockets dropped to 7-2, though they still own the best record in the West.

En total, el quinteto titular fue responsable de 99 de los 112 puntos de los 76ers. Los 76ers se adelantaron con un tiro libre de Embiid para el 17-18 a 3:40 del terminal el primer cuarto y ya no soltaron su ventaja hasta el final del partido. Ese intento de triple empañó un partido de Cunningham con 26 puntos, 11 asistencias y 7 rebotes. Duncan Robinson fue el máximo anotador de los Pistons con 27 puntos tras un excelente 7 de 11 desde el perímetro. Los 76ers sumaron la quinta victoria seguida y lideran el Este con un balance de 8-1 tras una única derrota encajada hace 10 días, precisamente, contra los Pistons. articles.title: Warriors coach Steve Kerr laughs at GOP midterms after begging reporters for political questions
articles.summary: Steve Kerr stopped reporters after practice at Chase Center to riff on midterm results, months after vowing to dial back his political takes.
articles.body: Golden State Warriors head coach Steve Kerr couldn’t help himself on Wednesday. Reporters at Chase Center were already packing up after practice. Recorders were off, notebooks were closed and nobody had asked about Washington. Kerr stopped the room anyway, asking why there were no questions on Tuesday’s midterms before launching straight into his routine. "I'm disappointed, because I was looking forward to that $5,000 check that we were all gonna get," Kerr said, taking a swipe at President Trump. "I already spent it, in fact. And I was so excited and sure about it that I spent it already. So now I'm gonna have to figure something out." THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Republicans had just gotten shellacked at the ballot box, and Kerr was dying to talk about it. Don't kid yourself: if Democrats had lost, he would’ve clammed up and kept politics far away from the microphone, just like he did with China. But with the GOP taking a beating, Kerr wasn't about to walk off without taking a victory lap. It's no secret Kerr is a bleed-blue lib, and midterm thumpings are par for the course. What made his post-practice comedy set so grating wasn't who won or lost on Tuesday. It was the shameless double standard on full display. STEVE KERR ADMITS HE WAS 'WRONG' ON HONG KONG, REGRETS CALLING TRUMP A 'BUFFOON' After endorsing Kamala Harris, taking the stage as a featured speaker at the Democratic National Convention, and co-opting Stephen Curry’s signature "night night" celebration to mock Donald Trump, Kerr suddenly tried to play the elder statesman. Even Warriors brass and league figures had grown visibly exhausted by the routine, with team owner Joe Lacob publicly conceding Kerr "sometimes goes a little far" with his political diatribes. Confronted with his own record, Kerr’s moral posturing dissolved into corporate cowardice. He admitted his silence on China’s atrocities in Hong Kong was transactional, aimed solely at protecting the NBA’s financial interests. To complete the convenient rebrand, he claimed he regretted calling Trump a "buffoon," piously lecturing that political debate should rise above the very insults he had spent years dishing out. The real issue is that Kerr loves playing political commentator only when he controls the script and faces zero pushback. When actually held to the facts, the highbrow disappears. Back in January, I pressed Kerr at Chase Center over his comments regarding federal immigration enforcement. After a road trip to Minnesota, he told reporters that ICE agents were not rooting out violent criminals, claiming instead that they were taking 5-year-old kindergartners and American citizens. Confronted with the agency's actual enforcement record and criminal arrest numbers, Kerr folded. "You're right, I definitely misspoke, and I knew that ICE was arresting some criminals," Kerr admitted. "I misspoke, and I apologize for the misinformation..." When I pressed for a follow-up question, Kerr shut down the exchange entirely, abruptly telling the room to move on: "All right, let's talk about basketball." OUTKICK IS NOW ON THE FOX APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD That pivot was his immediate exit ramp the moment he got caught spreading misinformation. He used the sport as a shield to kill the scrutiny. Yet on Wednesday, when a room full of sports reporters actually stuck to basketball, Kerr went out of his way to drag politics right back to the podium. If Kerr wants to treat the post-practice podium like his personal open-mic night, he can't cry foul and sprint back to basketball the second he gets fact-checked. articles.title: Victor Wembanyama makes NBA history with 52-point, 24-rebound, 8-block game in Spurs win
articles.summary: No player in NBA history has posted a game with those numbers.
articles.body:
Victor Wembanyama has had a heck of a career as he plays his fourth NBA season. But nothing matches what he did on Wednesday.

The San Antonio Spurs superstar set a new career high in scoring with 52 points plus 24 rebounds and 8 blocks in a 112-111 win over the Dallas Mavericks. No player in NBA history has posted those totals since blocks became an official stat in 1973, and only one other player had posted even a 50-20-5 game (Bob McAdoo, Feb 22, 1974).

The game came down to the final possessions, with Wembanyama making a free throw to give the Spurs the lead and Kyrie Irving missing a would-be game-winner right before the buzzer.

It was a tough shot for Irving, who had P.J. Washington unguarded on the perimeter but opted for a contested turnaround jump shot that missed the rim.

Wembanyama was clearly on pace for history from early in the game, eventually entering the locker room after becoming the first player to post at least 25 points, 15 rebounds and 5 blocks in a single half . It was a dominant half for both him and the Spurs, who led by 17 at halftime and as much as 19 in the third quarter.

The Mavericks, however, came back with Cooper Flagg and Naji Marshall leading the charge and at one point led by three in the fourth quarter. The Spurs were in dire straits around then, as Wembanyama briefly exited the game with an apparent ankle injury.

Wembanyama returned and helped the Spurs hold on. San Antonio outscored Dallas by 23 points during his 34 minutes, and got outscored by 22 in the 14 minutes back-up center Luke Kornet was playing.

Not only was Wembanyama temporarily hobbled, he also revealed after the game that he's been dealing with an illness . He said he was still sick Wednesday, but no longer felt as weak as he did while dealing with a virus:

"I haven't been feeling great lately. I've been sick. Today felt like I was getting my legs back. It should be more like this more often."

Wembanyama posted 12 points on 5-of-15 shooting with 11 rebounds, 5 assists and 3 blocks in his previous game, a win over the Utah Jazz. In the game directly before that, he dropped 43 in another win over the Minnesota Timberwolves. That was the second-highest scoring game of his career, and is now the third-highest.

The win improves the Spurs' record to 6-2, tied for fourth-best in a competitive Western Conference. The Mavericks are now tied for 10th at 4-4.

articles.title: Wemby's Historic Game Helps Spurs Beat Mavs, Box Score Stats & Highlights for Flagg, Kyrie, More
articles.summary: Victor Wembanyama is good at basketball.
articles.body:
Victor Wembanyama is good at basketball.

The San Antonio Spurs star put on a show while leading his team to a dramatic 112-111 victory over the Dallas Mavericks in Wednesday's Western Conference showdown at Frost Bank Center. The Spurs improved to 6-2 overall with their sixth straight win, while the Mavericks fell to 4-4 with a second consecutive loss.

Wembanyama wasted no time setting the tone with a historic first half on his way to a stunning performance of 52 points, 24 rebounds and eight blocks. Kyrie Irving did what he could for Dallas while Cooper Flagg passed Kevin Durant for points as a teenager, but it was all to no avail with the big man playing at such a level.

Irving had a chance to win it in the final seconds, but his jumper was off the mark.

Wednesday was an excellent opportunity for both teams to make an early statement. The Spurs could extend their winning streak, while the Mavericks had the chance to see how far they are from the NBA's elite with a measuring-stick game.

Elite was on full display from the start, as Wembanyama crossed up his defender in the opening minute and threw down a two-handed jam. It was a sign of what was to come, as he nearly notched a double-double in the first quarter alone.

Fittingly, he finished the quarter by getting out in transition, unleashing a quick move and slamming in another dunk. The reigning Defensive Player of the Year also swatted multiple shots and forced turnovers, allowing the Spurs to get out in transition as they built an early lead.

For as impressive as the dunks were, Wembanyama's blocks stood out even more as Dallas struggled to get anything going near the rim. He even blocked three shots in 13 seconds as the Spurs built a 17-point halftime advantage behind their star.

It was all part of one of the most impressive halves in NBA history.

The big man went into intermission with 29 points, 15 rebounds, five blocks and two steals as a one-man force on both ends of the floor. While Dylan Harper provided a scoring spark as well, the story was Wembanyama's brilliance.

Dallas could have gone through the motions in the second half facing such a dominant big man, but Irving kept the visitors within striking distance with his outside shooting and offensive aggressiveness. Flagg also put a terrible shooting start behind him, while P.J. Washington provided secondary scoring.

The Spurs' answer seemingly every time the Mavericks built any momentum was to just throw the ball up and let Wembanyama tower over defenders as he finished multiple alley-oops and continued to get to the free-throw line.

And still the Mavericks wouldn't go away.

Naji Marshall was key off the bench as the visitors continued to chip away at the lead. By the time Flagg finished an and-1 on an alley-oop and Washington drilled a three, the Mavericks were suddenly up three in front of a stunned crowd.

But the Spurs had Wembanyama and they didn't.

San Antonio continued to rely on its big man in crunch time, and he responded with a game-tying three and multiple baskets around the rim. He made what proved to be the winning free throw in the final minute, which was a fitting end to such a memorable performance.

articles.title: Mavericks’ Cooper Flagg climbs up all-time NBA list after surpassing Kevin Durant
articles.summary: Given how good Cooper Flagg already is, it’s easy to forget that he’s yet to turn 20 years of age. The 19-year-old, whose birthday is on December 21, 2006, i...
articles.body:
Given how good Cooper Flagg already is, it's easy to forget that he's yet to turn 20 years of age. The 19-year-old, whose birthday is on December 21, 2006, is blossoming into a legitimate superstar for the Dallas Mavericks right before our very eyes, and something higher up there than the sky appears to be the limit for him.

Flagg entered the night with 1,624 points to his name — having scored all of them as a teenager. This total had him tied with Kevin Durant for the fourth-most points scored by any NBA player aged 19 or younger. But by scoring on Wednesday against the San Antonio Spurs, Flagg moved in sole possession of fourth place, behind LeBron James (2,362), Kobe Bryant (1,759), and Cooper Flagg (1,725), as per ESPN Insights on X.

The Mavericks star entered their contest against the Spurs on Wednesday averaging 25.2 points, 5.7 rebounds, and 6.5 assists per game in his sophomore season. This is not the way a typical teenager produces in such a talented league as the NBA, and Flagg is lifting the Mavericks up with him.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Alas, even the best have their off-nights. Flagg, simply put, has not had it on Wednesday. He's been scuffling as of late; he scored 17 on just 3-of-19 shooting from the field on Monday in a loss to the Sacramento Kings, and he is following that up with another rough scoring night, putting up 11 points on 4-of-15 shooting through the third quarter of their clash against the Spurs.

Slumps are part of life, especially for a player as young as Flagg is. Nonetheless, he has plenty of time to pad his stats as a teenager. The Mavericks have 17 games (after this Spurs contest) left before Flagg turns 20, and if he averages around 25 points, his current season average, in those games, he will move to second all-time on the teenage NBA scoring list.

articles.title: Lakers win uneven game over Kings behind 40 points from Luka Doncic
articles.summary: Luka Doncic scores at least 40 points for third game in a row as the Lakers defeat the Sacramento Kings.
articles.body:
The Lakers encountered one of the NBA's least impressive teams in the Sacramento Kings on Wednesday night, making it incumbent on them to take the right approach against a team that has one of the worst records in the league .

Slowly, the Lakers and Luka Doncic found their groove against the Kings, pulling away for an uneven 116-103 win at Golden1 Center.

Doncic, of course, was at the center of it all, scoring 40 points to go with nine rebounds, seven assists and six turnovers. It was the third straight game Doncic has scored 40-plus points in an outing.

He had 10 points in the first quarter, a slow start for him considering he averages 15 points per game in the first 12 minutes. He had 13 in the second and 12 in the third and five in the fourth.

Walker Kessler had a strong game with 15 points on six-for-eight shooting, eight rebounds and three blocks.

The Kings began the game with a 1-6 record, one of six teams in the league with that mark.

They give up 124.3 points per game, the second-most in the league, and teams shoot 50.5% against them, a league-high.

So, the high-scoring Lakers just had to play to their usual effort.

They entered the game second in scoring (122.5) in the league and first in field-goal percentage (52.0).

But the first half was a choppy affair because of all the fouls being called.

Each team was called for 12 fouls in the first half. The Lakers were called for nine fouls in the second quarter and the Kings were called for eight.

Jake LaRavia picked up his fourth foul with eight minutes and two seconds left in the second quarter.

The Lakers had committed enough fouls to put the Kings in the penalty with 9:24 left in the second quarter.

That was the kind of first half the Lakers had to endure.

But when Doncic got going in the second quarter, the Lakers played a little better.

He scored 13 of their final 15 points in the half and had 23 points at intermission.

Kings sensational rookie guard Darius Acuff Jr., who is eighth in the NBA in scoring (26.1), had 14 points at the half, 22 for the game.

Doncic, however, entered the game as the top scorer in the league, averaging 38.3 points per game, and he ranked third in assists, averaging 8.1.

But this has been a season when Lakers coach JJ Redick said Doncic has provided the team more than just offense.

"Well, you brought up the leadership," Redick said. "I think that's where I've seen a lot of growth from him. Talking to his teammates…. We like to give that first minute to the players just to kind of talk to each other. And we've seen a lot of back and forth and it's been really healthy. So I love that from our team and from Luka. He's leading that right now."

Lakers forward Adou Thiero, who has been out with a left knee injury, practiced with the Coachella Valley Lakers on Wednesday and came out of well.

"Yeah, practice was fine today," Redick said. "Went well. That was the plan just to get him a live practice today and then he'll be back with us."

This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

articles.title: Luka Dončić has fan sitting courtside removed after incident with official during Lakers' win over Kings
articles.summary: Luka Dončić has now scored at least 40 points in five of his last six outings for the Lakers.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Lakers star Luka Dončić had a fan sitting courtside at the Golden 1 Center removed on Wednesday night after an incident between the fan and one of the game's officials.

As he was set to inbound the ball late in the third quarter of the Lakers' 116-103 win over the Sacramento Kings, Dončić suddenly started calling officials and security over on the baseline while pointing to a man sitting in a courtside seat. The man had caught the ball on the previous play and launched it back aggressively at the official, who was not prepared for it. The ball hit her awkwardly, which Dončić clearly didn't like.

"What the f*** are you doing?" Dončić appears to ask the fan before calling over others.

Officials stopped the game briefly and quickly approached the man. He was then walked out.

The game then continued on without incident. It's unclear if the man said anything back to Dončić.

The Lakers took a seven-point lead into the locker room at halftime, and then surged ahead in the second half to secure the 13-point win on Wednesday night. Dončić continued his offensive tear, and finished with 40 points, 9 rebounds and 7 assists. He shot 11 of 23 from the field. Dončić has scored at least 40 points in five of his last six outings, which includes a 52-point night late last month.

Austin Reaves added 21 points for the Lakers in the win. Walker Kessler finished with 15 points and eight rebounds. The Lakers now sit at 7-2 on the season.

Darius Acuff led the Kings with 22 points and 12 assists in the loss, which dropped them to 1-7 and 0-3 on their home court. Zach LaVine finished with 21 points, and Domantas Sabonis had 16 points and 17 rebounds.

Dončić and the Lakers will be back in action on Friday against the Portland Trail Blazers.

articles.title: ‘Absolutely no one’ – Nick Wright brutally calls out Stephen A. Smith over ‘political content’
articles.summary: Stephen A. Smith’s political commentary has been called out by his fellow sports analyst Nick Wright following the US midterm elections.
articles.body:
Stephen A. Smith's political commentary has been called out by his fellow sports analyst Nick Wright following the US midterm elections.

There was no NBA action on Tuesday night as the entire United States turned their attention to the midterm elections happening across the nation. This did not stop some of the NBA's most prominent voices from making themselves heard on the night, though.

Stephen A. Smith may be known for his takes on the NBA and NFL for the most part, but he has recently been quite active in the field of political commentary as well. Following the results, he released a video talking about how the Democrats' dominance might cost them in the next elections in 2028.

Nick Wright suggests Stephen A. Smith isn't 'being honest' with his audience in political commentary

ESPN's main man has been talking about politics for a significant amount of time at this point. There have even been suggestions that he might eventually run for political office himself. Although Smith has said in the past he would run as a Democrat if he had to, he has been known to also agree with the Republicans on various issues.

First Things First host Nick Wright took exception to Smith's take following the midterms, though, calling him out publicly in no uncertain terms.

"The problem with refusing to be honest with your audience (and potentially yourself!) about your politics while creating political content is you end up creating political content that appeals to… absolutely no one," Wright wrote in a post on X.

The current political climate in the country is quite tense, to say the least. Multiple issues being discussed in races have involved the sports world, albeit indirectly at times. Now it seems that even the bigger names in sports media are getting involved. Smith is unlikely to let this slide without response.

articles.title: Victor Wembanyama makes NBA history, matches Wilt Chamberlain with absurd statline
articles.summary: Victor Wembanyama had arguably his greatest NBA performance ever against the Dallas Mavericks, and he made NBA history by matching Wilt Chamberlain. Wilt Cha...
articles.body:
Victor Wembanyama had arguably his greatest NBA performance ever against the Dallas Mavericks, and he made NBA history by matching Wilt Chamberlain.

Wilt Chamberlain is the Mount Everest for single-game statistical records in the NBA. His dominance was so ridiculous that there are some fans today who refuse to believe it even happened. On Wednesday night, Victor Wembanyama showed any fans that stats like those can actually be achieved.

The San Antonio Spurs narrowly beat the Dallas Mavericks 112-111. This was despite an absolutely monstrous display by Wemby. He racked up 52 points, 24 rebounds, and eight blocks on a day where the opposition could simply do nothing about his greatness.

Victor Wembanyama becomes first player to achieve unique 52-24-8 statline, matches Wilt Chamberlain's record

While Wilt had games where he produced better numbers than this, Wembanyama became the first player in league history to achieve this particular statistical line. He did join Chamberlain as the only other player to have these sort of numbers, though.

"Only players in NBA history with 50+ PTS, 24+ REB and 8+ BLK in a single game: 1961 — Wilt Chamberlain. 2026 — Victor Wembanyama. Wemby joins WILT in the history books," DraftKings Sports shared on X.

Wembanyama was widely considered to be the frontrunner for the MVP award this season before it began. Luka Doncic's early dominance has since hampered those narratives, but this game is sure to put him right back on the map. When he plays like this, it is hard to suggest he is anything short of the best player in the world.

articles.title: How NBA is looking to turn India into a billion-dollar basketball market
articles.summary: New Delhi: For a league that has spent decades turning basketball players into global icons and team jerseys into fashion statements, the NBA's ambitions
articles.body: New Delhi: For a league that has spent decades turning basketball players into global icons and team jerseys into fashion statements, the NBA's ambitions in India were never going to be restricted to television screens. The challenge, however, is turning that appeal into a sustainable business.India, with its young population, expanding digital audience and growing appetite for global sports and entertainment, represents a significant long-term opportunity for the league. But the NBA is conscious that building a presence in a cricket-dominated market requires more than securing a broadcaster and hoping fans tune in to watch games played thousands of kilometres and many timezones away.It is looking to create multiple entry points for consumers, with basketball, fashion, music, entertainment and retail forming parts of a larger commercial strategy.The latest step in that direction is the expansion of its merchandising partnership with Indian apparel company Suditi. Having worked together since 2018, the two have extended their association, with Suditi taking over the operation of NBAStore.in in October 2026. The expanded portfolio includes casual shirts and lifestyle footwear, alongside jerseys, T-shirts, jackets, sweatshirts, headwear and accessories.More significantly, the partnership will see the NBA open its first physical store in India in 2027. It is an important development for a league looking to take its relationship with fans beyond digital engagement and into everyday consumption.The idea is to make NBA merchandise a lifestyle proposition rather than limit it to conventional sports apparel. Its teams, players and iconic jerseys already have recognition beyond basketball-following circles. Just look at numerous LA Lakers, Chicago Bulls, Michael Jordan, Steph Curry, LeBron James knockoffs that get sold in the local markets. The opportunity lies in converting that cultural appeal into official merchandise sales.Long-term commercial partnerships are another important part of the NBA's business model. Swiss watchmaker Tissot, which has been associated with the league for a decade, is an example of how these relationships can evolve beyond brand visibility."Our partnerships are built on shared values, a common vision and a commitment to evolving together. The decade-long NBA association exemplifies this, with both brands continually innovating to enhance fan experience, most recently through a redesigned shot clock now adopted across the WNBA," Tissot CEO Sylvain Dolla told TimesofIndia.com.Dolla added that the same approach extended to the brand's associations across basketball, cycling and motorsport, where it works with Swiss Timing to develop sport-specific solutions. "Our objective is to contribute to each sport's growth through long-term collaboration and innovation," he added.But retail and partnerships are only part of the equation.The NBA has spent considerable time experimenting with how Indian audiences consume its product. Its broadcast journey has included a decade-long association with Sony, followed by partnerships with MTV and digital platforms. It also explored making 100 games available live on YouTube, while its three-year association with Prasar Bharati took basketball content to DD Sports and a wider free-to-air audience.The reasoning was straightforward: live games alone cannot drive growth in a market where matches are played at inconvenient hours for Indian viewers."You can't just focus on broadcast and say, 'please watch my game.' You have to do other things around the sport," said Rajah Chaudhry, NBA's Asia-Pacific head of strategy, during an interaction with TimesofIndia.com in June."The objective is not to get cocooned into just one way of saying that live games are the way to be. We want to try different ways because people like to consume games in different ways in the country. That's our objective," added Sunny Malik, NBA India's Country Head.For the 2026-27 season, NBA games are available live in India on Prime Video and NBA League Pass. The challenge is to ensure that audiences remain connected to the league even when they are not watching live action.That is where digital content assumes importance. The NBA's Indian social media platforms have accumulated more than eight million followers, generating over 1.8 billion impressions and 1.35 billion video views. Highlights, short-form clips, player stories and locally produced content allow the league to remain part of the conversation throughout the year.Its approach to fan engagement also extends beyond the screen.BUDX NBA House, which moved from Mumbai to New Delhi in May this year, brings basketball together with music, fashion, celebrity appearances and entertainment. The format is particularly relevant in India, where the NBA's cultural appeal can reach audiences who may not necessarily follow the sport closely.The initiative has also found relevance beyond India, with elements of the experience informing the league's approach in other Asia-Pacific markets.There is, however, a distinction between building awareness and building a business. Social media numbers and event attendance offer encouraging signs, but converting occasional engagement into regular viewership, merchandise sales and long-term commercial partnerships remains the bigger test.Cricket continues to command the country's sporting attention, sponsorship money and broadcast market. The NBA also has to contend with a time-zone disadvantage and the challenge of developing a sizeable paying audience for a sport that still occupies a relatively small space in India's domestic sporting landscape.The league's India strategy, therefore, is built around connecting several businesses rather than relying on one. Broadcast distribution creates visibility, digital content sustains engagement, live experiences build communities, while merchandise and retail offer opportunities to monetise that relationship.The pieces are gradually falling into place. The question is whether they can come together to create something bigger.For the NBA, India's opportunity is not merely about getting more people to watch basketball. articles.body: l madrileño Hugo González disputó su tercer partido seguido como titular con los Boston Celtics de Joe Mazzulla en la victoria por 109-102 sobre los Milwaukee Bucks. González había sido titular en el triunfo sobre los Orlando Magic y la derrota contra los Houston Rockets. Contra los Bucks, González firmó 4 puntos tras un 1 de 3 en tiros de campo, 2 rebotes y un tapón con una sola pérdida en poco más de 14 minutos en pista. Paul George fue el máximo anotador de los Celtics con 25 puntos, mientras que Derrick White aportó 24. Tyler Herro y Jaime Jáquez Jr., dos ex Miami Heat que terminaron en Milwaukee con el traspaso de Giannis Antetokounmpo, firmaron 25 y 18 para los Bucks. Con esta titularidad, el canterano del Real Madrid igualó las tres que sumó la temporada pasada, la de su debut en la NBA, en la que empezó en tres de los 74 partidos que disputó. EF

articles.title: Wembanyama se exhibe con 52 puntos, 24 rebotes y 8 tapones
articles.standfirst: La hazaña de 'Wemby': un partido con más de 50 puntos, 20 rebotes y 5 tapones, es algo que solo habían logrado leyendas de este deporte como Wilt Chamberlain y Bob McAdoo
articles.summary: La hazaña de 'Wemby': un partido con más de 50 puntos, 20 rebotes y 5 tapones, es algo que solo habían logrado leyendas de este deporte como Wilt Chamberlain y Bob McAdoo
articles.body: El pívot francés Victor Wembanyama firmó una actuación al alcance de muy pocos en la historia de la NBA, con 52 puntos, 24 rebotes y 8 tapones, en una noche que también supuso su nuevo récord anotador en la liga. Wembanyama, además, fue autor de la canasta decisiva del partido, un tiro libre a 24 segundos del final que dio la victoria por 112-111 a los San Antonio Spurs ante los Dallas Mavericks en el Frost Bank Center de San Antonio. La hazaña de 'Wemby': un partido con más de 50 puntos, 20 rebotes y 5 tapones, es algo que solo habían logrado leyendas de este deporte como Wilt Chamberlain y Bob McAdoo. Wembanyama sumó sus 52 puntos con 16 de 28 tiros de campo (aunque solo anotó uno de sus ocho intentos de triple) y 19 de 23 tiros libres. Sus 24 rebotes se repartieron en 15 defensivos y 9 ofensivos. Y además de los 8 tapones, repartió dos asistencias y robó dos balones. Una auténtica exhibición de un jugador que había dejado su récord anotador en 50 puntos hace dos temporadas. El francés, 2,24 metros, acumula 58 partidos con al menos cinco tapones desde que debutó en la liga. Pese a esta destacada actuación, los Spurs lo pasaron mal para imponerse a los Mavericks, sobre todo en los minutos finales, después de que un parcial de 0-10 de Dallas redujera a dos puntos una ventaja que había llegado a ser de 19 para San Antonio. Un triple de P.J. Washington llegó a poner a los Maverciks por delante 100-103, pero Wembanyama le respondió con otro en el siguiente ataque para frenar la remontada visitante. Irving estuvo cerca de aguarle la fiesta a Wembanyama en la última posesión del partido, pero falló el tiro que hubiese dado el triunfo a los Mavericks. A Wembanyama le acompañaron Dylan Harper con 21 puntos y Stephon Castle con 17. Para los Mavericks, Kyrie Irving firmó 27 puntos, Naji Marshall 22, Washington firmó un doble-doble con 21 puntos y 10 rebotes, números muy parecidos a los de Cooper Flagg, con 19 puntos y 10 rebotes. Los Spurs (6-2), que comenzaron la temporada con dos derrotas, encadenan ahora seis victorias consecutivas. EFE

articles.title: Aday Mara se estrena como titular con los Thunder

articles.summary: Además de sus 9 puntos y 5 rebotes, Mara repartió dos asistencias y puso tres tapones en casi 25 minutos en pista.
articles.body: El 'rookie' español Aday Mara se estrenó como titular con los Oklahoma City Thunder, que se impusieron por 124-116 a los Cleveland Cavaliers con 9 puntos y 5 rebotes del pívot aragonés. Además de sus 9 puntos y 5 rebotes, Mara repartió dos asistencias y puso tres tapones en casi 25 minutos en pista. Mara formó quinteto con Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Ajay Mitchell, Isaiah Hartenstein y Kenrich Williams. Gilgeous-Alexander terminó con 42 puntos el partido. Las lesiones de Jalen Williams y Cason Wallace, y sobre todo la de Chet Holmgren, han abierto a Mara las puertas de la titularidad en los Thunder. El pívot aragonés fue elegido por la franquicia de Oklahoma City en el número 12 del último 'draft'. Mara promedia 6,8 puntos y 5,5 rebotes en este arranque de liga, hasta este miércoles como suplente. En apenas ocho partidos, el 'rookie' ha firmado ya su primer doble-doble. La titularidad de Mara en Oklahoma City coincidió este miércoles con la de otro español, Hugo González, en Boston con los Celtics. González, en su segundo año en la NBA, acumula tres titularidades seguidas a las órdenes de Joe Mazzulla. EFE

articles.title: NBA: Victor Wembanyama scores career-high 52 points as San Antonio Spurs beat Dallas Mavericks
articles.summary: Victor Wembanyama sinks the winning free throw to finish with a career-high 52 points as the San Antonio Spurs beat the Dallas Mavericks 112-111.
articles.body:
Victor Wembanyama sank the winning free throw to finish with a career-high 52 points as the San Antonio Spurs beat the Dallas Mavericks 112-111 on Wednesday.

The French star, whose previous best was 50 points in 2024, dominated at both ends of the court to also claim 24 rebounds and eight blocks.

The 22-year-old is the first player in 52 years with at least 50 points, 20 rebounds and five blocks in a game.

He also became the fifth player since 1982 to register at least 50 points and 20 rebounds as San Antonio improved their record to 6-2.

Wembanyama reached half-time with 29 points, 15 rebounds, five blocks and two steals, before the Spurs held off a second-half rally by Dallas, who were led by 29 points from Kyrie Irving.

"I haven't been feeling great lately," said Wembanyama. "I've been sick for a while.

"Today I felt like I got my legs back, so it should be more like this more often."

Jaylen Brown and Joel Embiid led the Philadelphia 76ers to a 112-106 win over the Detroit Pistons in their top-of-the-table Eastern Conference clash.

Brown (30 points) and Embiid (26) led a balanced offensive performance as Philadelphia saw all five starters reach double figures, with LeBron James claiming a double-double of 13 points and 10 rebounds.

The 76ers now have the NBA's best record at 8-1 after bringing in Brown and James in the off-season.

"It's too early to be talking about the Finals and things of that nature," said James. "We'll just continue to buy into what we want to do. We got a good team."

The Los Angeles Lakers beat the Sacramento Kings 116-103 with Luka Doncic scoring a game-high 40 points to reach 308 for the season.

The Slovenian star became the first player to pass 300 in his first eight games of a season since Michael Jordan (303) in 1988-89.

Doncic was also involved in an incident which led to a fan being removed after throwing the ball at an official, which struck her as she was signalling a Lakers possession.

Meanwhile, London-born OG Anunoby scored 18 points for the New York Knicks as the reigning champions enjoyed their biggest win of the season, beating the Chicago Bulls 135-105 to improve to 4-4.

articles.title: Wembanyama overcomes illness, injury in historic outing as Spurs top Mavs for sixth straight win
articles.summary: Victor Wembanyama was battling a virus, rolled his ankle in the fourth quarter and does not believe he is playing his best.
articles.body: SAN ANTONIO — Victor Wembanyama was battling a virus, rolled his ankle in the fourth quarter and does not believe he is playing his best. All of which made the San Antonio Spurs star’s historic outing against the Dallas Mavericks even that more astounding. After establishing a league milestone in the first half, Wembanyama finished with career highs of 52 points and 24 rebounds along with eight blocks to lead the Spurs past the Mavericks 112-111 on Wednesday night. Wembanyama had 29 points, 15 rebounds and five blocks in the first half to become the first player since the NBA’s play-by-play era began in 1996-1997 with at least 25 points, 10 rebounds and five blocks in a half. “He’s Superman,” Spurs point guard Dylan Harper said. “I mean, he rolls his ankle and pops right up and acts like nothing happened. I’ve never seen nothing like that, but that’s just a testament to how he takes care of his body, how he focuses on his mobility, treatment, all that. So he’s able to do things like that.” San Antonio was plus-23 when Wembanyama was on the court. The 7-foot-4 center from France was 16 for 28 from the field, including seven dunks, but 1 for 8 on 3-pointers. “I can still do more,” Wembanyama said. “I mean, my shots weren’t falling tonight and that forces me into a style of play that is exhausting. I can do it. I mean the proof is here. I can do it, but I can be much better if my shots fall. I know it’s just a matter of time.” Still, three days after being named the Western Conference Player of the Week, Wembanyama presented a strong case for a repeat. “I hope so,” Wembanyama said. “The goal is to get it every week.” The Spurs have won six straight and swept a three-game homestand. San Antonio has not lost since dropping the season’s first two games to Oklahoma City and Houston. Wembanyama has averaged 32.5 points during the streak despite being under the weather with a virus. “I haven’t been feeling great lately,” Wembanyama said. “I’ve been sick for a while and today I felt like I got my legs back. So it should be more like this, more often.” He certainly looked spry to open the game. Wembanyama scored 10 of San Antonio’s first 12 points, powering down two dunks and draining all six free-throw attempts. He closed the first quarter with 15 points, nine rebounds, two blocks, two steals and an assist. After capturing his ninth rebound, Wembanyama dribbled behind his back at Dallas’ 3-point line to avoid Walter Clayton Jr., drove between two defenders for a one-handed dunk and then stood in the paint screaming in celebration. “He was making an impact for his team,” said Mavericks guard Kyrie Irving, who missed a 15-footer with three seconds remaining. “You can see his aggression has been raising over the past few games.” The onslaught continued in the second quarter. Wembanyama had three blocks in 13 seconds on the same possession, sending shots by Cooper Flagg and P.J. Washington flying out of bounds before his third was captured by De’Aaron Fox with 3:38 remaining in the first half. Wembanyama rolled his ankle after stepping on Clayton’s foot, exiting with 9:11 remaining in the game. He spent the next several minutes stretching his foot and ankle on the bench before returning with 6:05 remaining. “I mean the moment that stands out for some reason. I don’t have any agenda I want to say, but it’s when I rolled my ankle,” Wembanyama said. The Spurs certainly needed their All-Star in the final minutes. Wembanyama had two putbacks in the final 2:39. He missed his first three free throws in the final 2:10, but made one with 24 seconds left for the final margin of victory.

articles.title: El centenario Doncic hereda el legado de Kobe y supera a Jordan: "Es uno de los mejores de la historia"
articles.standfirst: Luka Doncic suma tres partidos anotando al menos 40 puntos, seis con al menos 35 puntos, 5 rebotes, 5 asistencias y 5 triples y supera una marca anotadora de Michael Jordan
articles.summary: Luka Doncic suma tres partidos anotando al menos 40 puntos, seis con al menos 35 puntos, 5 rebotes, 5 asistencias y 5 triples y supera una marca anotadora de Michael Jordan
articles.body: Los Angeles Lakers, liderados por Luka Doncic (40 puntos (6 de 13 en triples y 12 de 13 tiros libres)), 9 rebotes y 7 asistencias) ganaron 103-116 a los Sacramento Kings en uno de los derbis de California en la NBA. Doncic, que suma tres partidos seguidos con 40 puntos o más, ha registrado al menos 35 puntos, 5 rebotes, 5 asistencias y 5 triples en seis partidos consecutivos, superando la marca de Damian Lillard (2020) y estableciendo la racha más larga en la historia de la NBA. El ex del Real Madrid se consolida con el máximo anotador del curso en la NBA con un promedio de 38,5 puntos por partido. Zach LaVine, que anotó 21 puntos en la derrota de los Kings, no dudó en elogiar a Doncic: "Luka es uno de los jugadores con más talento de todos los tiempos. No creo que la gente le dé el suficiente reconocimiento por lo bueno que es realmente. Es uno de los mejores anotadores de la historia". Doncic suma 308 puntos en los primeros 8 partidos de la temporada 2026-2027 de la NBA, frente a los 303 puntos que sumó Michael Jordan en los primeros 8 partidos de la 88-89. El único jugador que ha anotado más puntos en sus primeros ocho partidos de una temporada es Wilt Chamberlain, quien lo consiguió en tres ocasiones, alcanzando un máximo de 418 puntos en sus primeros ocho encuentros de la temporada 1962-63. Luka Doncic, que disputó su partido 100 con Los Angeles Lakers, fue preguntado en rueda de prensa sobre sus similitudes competitivas con Kobe Bryant. "Es un gran honor. Creo que todos sabemos quién fue Kobe Bryant y lo que significó para todo el mundo, especialmente en el ámbito del baloncesto. Fue un ídolo para muchas personas, así que significa mucho que se me mencione junto a su nombre", declaró el ex del Real Madrid. Con Doncic como líder los Lakers suman siete victorias en nueve partidos. Luka Doncic ayudó a que un aficionado sentado a pie de pista fuera expulsado. "Simplemente lanzó el balón con mucha fuerza a la árbitra. Sólo le pregunté qué demonios estaba haciendo", contó el ex del Real Madrid.

articles.title: 7 NBA Players Most Likely To Be Traded This Season
articles.summary: We've got a full three months until the 2027 NBA trade deadline, but we already have a pretty good idea of which players will become topics of discussion between now and then.
articles.body:
We've got a full three months until the 2027 NBA trade deadline, but we already have a pretty good idea of which players will become topics of discussion between now and then.

Kyrie Irving has been his usual spectacular self for the Dallas Mavericks, helping unlock a leveled-up version of Cooper Flagg. But we all know there's no real future for those two together; Irving is 14 years older than his ascending teammate and is Dallas' best tool to replenish its empty asset cupboard.

Meanwhile, Kristaps Porzingis isn't going to contribute in Golden State. Norman Powell was basically signed to be traded. Anthony Davis, without an extension, will command serious interest in Washington if he stays healthy.

Let's check in on those players and a handful of others who seem destined to wind up in the rumor mill when trade season rolls around.

The Brooklyn Nets are one of the only teams we can still evaluate using the rules of the previous lottery system. Bottoming out is a bad move for most, but the Nets have to swap their 2027 first-rounder with the Houston Rockets and should actually want to finish with one of the three worst records in the league.

That'll both devalue the pick going to Houston and also marginally increase their chance to maximize the value of the 2028 first-rounder they actually control.

That's all to say that stripping off talent is still a good move here. Michael Porter Jr. is on an expiring $40.8 million salary and should be highly sought after by contenders in need of elite shooting at forward. If the Nets aren't going to extend him, they'd better get something for him ahead of unrestricted free agency this summer.

Brooklyn isn't incentivized to win this season, so shopping a veteran starter who's on his way to averaging over 20.0 points per game with excellent efficiency for the second year in a row should be a top priority.

Every argument you could make in favor of Dallas keeping Kyrie Irving also cuts the other way.

Irving is playing virtually the same brand of masterful offensive basketball he did before tearing his ACL. He's at least partially responsible for Cooper Flagg's ascent. Seems compelling, right? Well, doesn't Irving's success and impact also mean his trade value is pretty high right now? Shouldn't the Mavs be keenly aware that Irving's age (34) and injury history indicate the good times aren't guaranteed to last?

It's tempting to just keep Irving and Flagg together for as long as possible, but the precariousness of Irving's form urges action. Bigger picture: The 14-year age gap between the two means the partnership was always going to have a short shelf life.

Dallas is woefully lean on draft capital. Moving Irving could be the best way to change that. If Flagg is going to be as great as his early-season work suggests, he'll need age-appropriate help and a team with the flexibility to get it. Irving is a means to that end, even if he's been undeniably good to start the year.

Kristaps Porzingis, Golden State Warriors

The moment another team decides it would like to send the Golden State Warriors a middling asset in exchange for $17 million in 2027-28 savings, expect a deal to get done.

Oh, right: That $17 million in savings has a name. It's Kristaps Porzingis.

The veteran center inked a two-year, $40 million deal to stick with the Dubs this past offseason. Because Porzingis' availability has been (at best) sporadic over the last handful of seasons, the Warriors limited their downside risk by guaranteeing only $3 million of a possible $20 million next year.

In effect, Porzingis is a $20 million expiring salary that the organization was always prepared to treat as a trade chip.

Lest there be any confusion over Porzingis' standing with the team after he waited until the 11th hour to inform them he wouldn't report to training camp, ESPN's Anthony Slater submitted a report that clarified where everyone stands.

Per Slater: "Team sources continue to express an extreme level of pessimism that Porzingis will ever play for the Warriors again."

Porzingis may not play for anyone else either, but Golden State will be highly motivated to turn him into a pick or a player who'll actually suit up.

Norman Powell is 33 and still filling it up. The veteran guard is on track to average over 20.0 points per game for the third straight year, though his scoring exploits haven't really driven much success for the Chicago Bulls.

That's fine. The Bulls didn't ink Powell to a two-year, $44 million deal because they expected him to put them over the top competitively. Instead, his contract is a shrewd example of asset management.

The second year of Powell's contract is a team option, basically catnip to contenders in search of rentals and flexibility. Powell's age, then, is just one factor that makes him a short-timer on a Bulls squad that is finally rebuilding. His effectively expiring contract is the other.

Powell was never much of a defender on the wing. Age has further diminished him in that regard, but it's not like he's earning two-way star money. At just 13.0 percent of the cap this year, Powell could easily slot into a high-scoring sixth-man role for a team that needs spacing and has a defensive infrastructure that can minimize his weaknesses.

If you had to bet on one player jumping from a lottery team to a playoff-bound outfit by the deadline, you'd almost have to pick Powell.

The Washington Wizards lost their negotiating resolve when it came to Trae Young, but they found it in time to hold strong with Anthony Davis. The oft-injured big man didn't get an offseason extension and will either hit unrestricted free agency in 2027 or pick up his $63 million player option.

When a team allows a player as costly as Davis to reach this point, it tends to force action.

Davis might have his eye on another organization more willing to pay him than the Wizards. Meanwhile, Washington probably doesn't love the idea of AD declining his option and leaving for nothing in free agency.

All it cost the Wizards to acquire Davis was a "meh" matching salary, the No. 30 pick in 2026 and a top-20 protected 2030 first-rounder, which means their asking price probably won't be high. AD's salary isn't easy for most teams to take on, but one imagines a deal to the Warriors for Jimmy Butler's expiring money and a pick would get it done.

Washington won't commit to Davis on a long-term extension and shouldn't risk watching him walk. We all know how these kinds of stories typically end.

Derrick Jones Jr. leads a list of affordable veterans the rebuilding LA Clippers need to move prior to the trade deadline. An athletic lob threat who has shot at least 35.0 percent from deep for three straight years, Jones is still mobile enough at 29 to wrangle the toughest perimeter matchups.

His expiring $10.5 million salary makes the two-way forward a huge value. It doesn't hurt that he showed the ability to contribute during deep playoff runs in Dallas and Miami earlier in his career.

Jones may not be worth a first-rounder in a trade on his own, but the Clippers could aggregate his salary with those of Max Strus (16.7 million), Brook Lopez (9.2 million) or Kris Dunn ($5.6 million) to send out a significant number. LA shouldn't necessarily be in the business of taking on a huge contract, but that might be the right move if it comes with draft capital attached.

Although the Clippers hauled in two future first-rounders in the deal that sent Kawhi Leonard to Toronto, they're still down five picks they surrendered to the league for cap circumvention.

Jones and the rest of LA's reasonably priced vets can help the team get back to even on the draft-asset front.

The Milwaukee Bucks present a real challenge—not for opposing teams on the court, but for those of us tasked with isolating the player they're most likely to move.

Tyler Herro has an expiring $33 million salary and appeal as an All-Star scorer to teams seeking a rentable offensive boost. That puts him narrowly ahead of teammates who should also draw trade interest as the Bucks try to recoup draft assets and rebuild in a post-Giannis Antetokounmpo era.

Herro is a Wisconsin product who might prefer to stick around. He's playing that way so far. While it's not news that he's racking up 20 points per game for the sixth straight season, it's worth noting that he's never done it more efficiently. He won't make nearly half of his threes all year, but the ones he's hit so far certainly count, as teams around the league should take notice.

The Bucks also have Kyle Kuzma ($20.5 million) and Caris LeVert ($14.8 million) to dangle as expiring salaries, not to mention Myles Turner and a slew of rookie-scale pieces that came from Miami.

Even 2025-26 breakout guard Ryan Rollins is a trade candidate because his $4 million salary is too small for Milwaukee to extend off of before free agency via a declined player option this summer.

The league will be blowing up Milwaukee's phones from now until February. Herro won't be the only player dealt, but he's probably the most likely of the group.
